summary: SL-103 was filed as a minor, four-row widening of the OpenSubKey write marker. The class obligation turned it into a full enumeration of Explorer\Advanced write spellings. Four src patterns (yaml plus Fact) and six rule-C patterns were widened in place, so the 6/9 counts and the parity line stayed unchanged. ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json went from 63 to 124 rows and gained bounded_by, aliases, census and closed_by. Twelve harness plants were added, and the suite is 935/935. The pre-fix proof is repeatable: 42 ids fail at 1105c3f, not the 33 the design predicted. Code review still found five more members of the provider-cmdlet and reg.exe families after the build called them closed. Those were waived to the backlog, and validate then measured four of them as real writes.

payload.reason: Reflection on SL-103 (follow-up 2 deep, so no candidates land). All numbers come from the stage records above; I re-ran nothing.

payload.estimate_error: Opened medium / low risk, sized by a person. Medium was right: 10 files changed, 61 rows added, 12 plants, +61 tests. Low risk was right: the defect is latent, with zero registry calls in src/ or tests/window/, and the widened patterns added no stray hit on today's tree. The brief understated the work. It named one marker in three places and four rows (B30, B31, B32, W35), while the class obligation produced 61 new rows and in-place edits to 4 of 6 src patterns (two copies) and 6 of 9 rule-C patterns. Accepted review findings M1 and M2 grew the before-fix failing set from the design's 33 to 42 ids and the planned 46 rows to 61. The loop also needed more laps than a low-risk slice implies: build-check, critique and code-review each ran twice.

learned.lesson: Enumerate a PowerShell or reg.exe family from the tool, not from the finding's examples. List the verbs of Get-Command -Module Microsoft.PowerShell.Management for *-Item and *-ItemProperty, and the verbs of `reg /?`. Give each verb a fire, miss or out row in the census at design time. Here the family was patched example by example and kept reopening.
learned.evidence: Critique M1 named New-Item/Clear-Item/Copy-/Move-/Rename-ItemProperty. Code-review round 1 then found Rename-Item, Move-Item, Rename-ItemProperty -NewName and reg copy. Round 2 found New-Item -Path <parent> -Name Advanced (O-017 declared the family closed; waived as O-024, O-025, O-028).

learned.lesson: A waiver graded 'minor' or 'does not weigh a lap' on a guard hole says nothing about whether the write is real. Validate measured four waived members as real writes in the Sandbox. SC-311, SC-313, SC-314 and SC-315 should be treated as confirmed members, not hypotheticals, when they are picked up.
learned.evidence: Validate-slice: '[failed] Waived members O-024, O-025, O-026 and O-028 are real writes (backlog evidence, Sandbox)'.

learned.lesson: The corpus census, aliases and bounded_by.member text are prose over row ids that nothing checks (m3 waived, SC-308). Any slice that edits ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json should first add the assertion to TheCorpusHoldsRowsTheDeclaredPatternsLetThroughInBothScopes: every id named in census, aliases or closed_by exists with the stated verdict, and every fire or miss row is named in census. Until then the build's one-off throwaway script is the only check, and bounded_by.member can name spellings the rows do not cover.
learned.evidence: Code-review round 1: bounded_by.member names moving, renaming and copying as members while the census omits them. Build left-open: 'Review m3 (waived, SC-308) ... checked once at build time by a throwaway script'.

learned.lesson: The 9 window and 6 src pattern counts are asserted (ExplorerSettingsWriteRuleTests.cs:83-84), and each rule-C pattern must stay one single-quoted yaml line for SettledPatterns. Every widening therefore piles alternatives into :1124/:1126/:1130. The next widening of rule C is the point to take the filed AST route (#400) rather than add a fifth alternative.
learned.evidence: Design: 'Widen patterns in place and add none'. Build: :1124 now carries the ItemProperty verb list plus a Remove-Item/New-Item/Clear-Item lookaround group. :1130 carries four alternatives (true marker, rights enum, quoted string, flags string).

learned.lesson: The taad_v3 Fitness engine reads files as UTF-8 with errors=replace (backend/taad3/fitness.py:445). A UTF-16LE .reg file, which is what `reg export` writes, is invisible to every content pattern. That is why W53 and W54 are pinned miss. Do not design .reg-content rules until the engine decodes by BOM, which is outside this repo.
learned.evidence: Risk spike reg-import-and-reg-content-patterns (no-go): adv-utf16.reg 0 hits, adv-utf8.reg 2.

learned.lesson: Runtime measurement outranked the issue text twice. A RegistryRights.CreateSubKey handle cannot write (RegSetValueExW=5), so CreateSubKey is not a marker and B38 is quiet. A quoted string second argument binds OpenSubKey(string,bool) as $true in PowerShell, so 'ReadKey' and 'False' open the key writable. Validate then recorded the CreateSubKey deviation as 'criterion not met' while the slice passed, with no person decision on it. Next time a measured deviation from the issue text should be put to a person as a question before build.
learned.evidence: Investigation S3 (state=4 for 'False'; Hidden 2->1 for W36-W38/W46). Validate 'criterion not met: Issue text: widen the marker to include CreateSubKey'.

learned.lesson: A build-check criterion that records 'the bug is present today' comes back `present`, and the aggregate verdict then reads `partial` and halts the stage even though all the work is still missing. The first build-check halted for this and the second 'built anyway', so the lap added nothing. Write premise checks as context, not as graded criteria.
learned.evidence: Build-check #1 halted ('dropped from the reply ... Baseline ... present ... read as partial'). Build-check #2 'built anyway despite a partial survey'.

learned.lesson: Size a 'close the class' follow-up from the census, not from the filing's example rows. This slice went from 4 named rows to 61 added rows (124 total) and 12 plants. The expected before-fix failing set moved 33 -> 42 as accepted findings added rows after the design fixed its counts. Re-derive the expected failing-id list after the critique disposes of its findings, not at design time.
learned.evidence: Build: 'before-fix failing set is 42 ids, not the design's 33: B50 and W60-W67 from accepted review findings M1 and M2'. Design said 46 rows; 61 were added.

learned.lesson: All 12 findings of this slice (7 critique, 5 code-review) were answered by a model. None was triaged by a person, so the critique, critique-review and code-review gates have no measured precision here. critique-review did not run (low risk, minimal project) and recorded nothing. The only independent signal on the gates is missed[], which is why it matters.
learned.evidence: Critique #2: '7 answered by a model, counted as untriaged'. Code-review #2: '5 answered by a model'. Critique-review #1: sizing skip.

learned.lesson: Validate's run-time evidence is weaker than it reads. The Sandbox runs as SYSTEM under Windows PowerShell 5.1 on build 26100. The key-level rows (Remove-Item, DeleteSubKeyTree, New-Item -Force, Rename-Item, Move-Item) were refused on SYSTEM's real key and measured on a scratch key of the same shape. pwsh 7, Windows 10 and an ordinary user's own HKCU are unmeasured. The guard verdicts do not depend on this, but 'member' claims for key-level rows do.
learned.evidence: Validate 'not reached' list: ordinary user's HKCU, pwsh 7, Windows 10, effective setting re-read after each write.

lessons_judged.why: The design wrote 'bounded by producer, known misses pinned', not 'class closed', and filed the AST/analyser route for the next reopening. Code review still found five more regex-uncovered members, which confirms the lesson. O-017's 'closed as the class' discharge was the wording it warns against.

The design and corpus census were built around the full API family (open, set, delete, import, cmdlets), not the one OpenSubKey instance. Critique M1 still said the design 'repeats #225' for the provider cmdlets, and code review found more siblings, so the lesson applied but the enumeration was not exhaustive.

The decision on R2-m5 refused the critic's suggested New-Item `-Name Advanced` regex because it would fire on any folder named Advanced, and required an Explorer lookahead plus a quiet filesystem row. M2's widened text was run against all 124 rows in Fitness and xUnit before ship.

It shaped every new pattern to be single-line, using [ \t] and [^\r\n]. Critique m5 cited it and asked for a multi-line plant, but that plant was waived (SC-310). Validate lists the real multi-line layout as 'not reached', so only half of the lesson was acted on.

The slice was sized medium by a person and needed corpus, harness and rule-rewrite work: 10 files, +61 tests, 12 plants. It matches the lesson's prediction that a 'one-line' fix becomes a corpus slice.

The design read fitness.yaml and rules-parity first. It recorded that rule C is settled (below '# settled by SL-091') and is never compared by parity, and that architecture_rules would only add a settled third copy, so it declared none.

Because of RuleCases' hard-coded parity line, patterns were widened in place so the line stays 'AGREE 18 facts <- 22 twinned entries, 48 patterns; 69 settled'. RuleCases C-001/C-003/C-004/C-005 were run at build, code review and validate.
The design chose empty architecture_rules deliberately to stop the engine appending a settled third copy of the guards, and cited this lesson's mechanism.

The harness command and --engine-root were used with --only on 16 plants, and every run read CLEAN with all rows AS-RECORDED. Its numbers are stale: the clean baseline is now 91 rules and 225 files, not 17 rules.

Validate here did have the engine interpreter. It ran rules-parity, RuleCases C-001/3/4/5 and the rules-harness under %APPDATA%\taad3\venv Python, all passing. The 'validate has no engine interpreter' premise did not hold on this slice.
All builds and tests went through eng/dotnet.ps1. The first survey installed SDK 10.0.401 into the gitignored .dotnet/ because the host has none, and the repo-local SDK was reused after that.

what_went_wrong: Build-check halted on its first pass because a premise criterion ('the bug is present today') came back present and made the whole survey read `partial`. The second pass 'built anyway' with no new information, so the lap was wasted.

O-017 was discharged as 'closed as the class registry-provider cmdlets'. Code review then found Rename-Item, Move-Item, Rename-ItemProperty -NewName and (second round) New-Item -Path <parent> -Name Advanced getting 0 hits. This is the failure lessons #225 and #400 warned about, and it happened with both handed in. Each review round fixed the verbs it named and left the next sibling.

Five code-review findings were waived to the backlog as minor (O-024 to O-028: SC-311, SC-312, SC-313, SC-314, SC-315). Validate then measured O-024, O-025, O-026 and O-028 as real writes in the Sandbox. The slice passed while its own validation recorded known producer-made holes in a guard the corpus describes as 'bounded by producer'.

The corpus's bounded_by.member names moving, renaming and copying as members, but neither the rows nor the census covered them. The build wrote that text without checking it against the rows, and only code review caught the contradiction.

The design's expected failing-id set (33 ids, 46 rows) was wrong by the end: 42 ids, 61 rows. The design froze counts before the critique's accepted M1/M2 findings added B50 and W60-W67. The build declared this, but the design's 'exactly 33' check could not have held.
Fixes the slice declared as follow-ups were not done: docs/design/SL-091-hidden-reveal-refuses.md still calls both guards 'closed as a class', contradicting the corpus and both `because` texts.

The issue text asked for CreateSubKey in the marker and the build-check named it (C1). The measurement showed it cannot write, and the build dropped it. Validate recorded 'criterion not met' while passing the slice, with no recorded decision from a person on the deviation.
All 12 findings were disposed of by a model, and critique-review was skipped by sizing without an account. The gates' precision on this slice is unmeasured.

missed.what: The critique named registry-provider cmdlets in M1 but enumerated only the verbs it had seen (New/Clear-Item, Copy/Move/Rename-ItemProperty). It never listed Get-Command -Module Microsoft.PowerShell.Management for *-Item and *-ItemProperty. Rename-Item, Move-Item and Rename-ItemProperty -Name HiddenOld -NewName Hidden therefore passed rule C. The existing :1125 `-Name` handling cannot see -NewName, and the lookaround group at :1124 does not list Rename-Item or Move-Item. Check to write: every verb of the provider cmdlet module has a fire, miss or out row in the census.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 1 (O-024, waived as SC-313; validate measured the members as real writes)

missed.what: The reg.exe census listed only add, delete and import. It was never checked against the `reg /?` verb list (query, add, delete, copy, save, restore, load, unload, compare, export, import, flags). `reg copy <backup> <Explorer\Advanced> /s /f` works unelevated on HKCU and writes Hidden back, but rule C's :1126 gets 0 hits.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 1 (O-025, waived as SC-314; validate measured it as a real write)

missed.what: When M1 added New-Item to rule C, the critique asked only about the form with Explorer\Advanced adjacent on the line. It did not ask for the documented -Path <parent> -Name 'Advanced' -Force spelling, which recreates the key empty exactly as W60 does. :1124 needs adjacency, so the line gets 0 hits. Check to write: for each cmdlet added to a path-adjacency pattern, feed the -Path/-Name split spelling.

The critique checked argument spellings of the OpenSubKey call but not how reg.exe is launched. This repo launches native programs through Start-Process -ArgumentList and ArgumentList.Add (WindowCases.ps1:473, :685, :5743). `Start-Process reg.exe -ArgumentList 'import',$file` and `& reg @('add',$adv,'/v','Hidden',...)` get 0 hits from :1126, which needs whitespace and the verb right after `reg`.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 1 (O-026, waived as SC-311; validate measured it as a real write)

missed.what: The critique and design fired named-argument opens (B08 `writable: true`, B37 `rights: RegistryRights.SetValue`) but did not ask the same question of the value-name patterns. `key.DeleteValue(name: "Hidden")` and `key.SetValue(name: "Hidden", value: 1)` get 0 hits, because the src patterns need the quote directly after `(`. The bound was inconsistent and unpinned.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 1 (O-027, waived to SC-312 and pinned only as a decision to add a miss row)

unknowns: Can an ordinary user's own HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced be removed, renamed, moved or recreated by Remove-Item, Rename-Item, Move-Item or New-Item -Force? SYSTEM's key refused all of them for an unpinned reason and only a scratch key was measured. That decides whether the key-level rows (W49, W50, W60 and the SC-313/SC-315 shapes) are real members for the producer.

Does PowerShell 7 bind a quoted string second argument to OpenSubKey(string, bool) as $true, like Windows PowerShell 5.1? W36, W37, W38 and W46 (fire rows) were measured writable only on 5.1. Round 1 measured identical handle behaviour on pwsh 7.6 / .NET 10.0.12, but not the string-to-bool overload binding.
Will the taad_v3 Fitness engine ever decode UTF-16 by BOM (fitness.py:445)? Until it does, W53 and W54 stay miss rows and no .reg-content pattern can be adopted. The change lives outside this repo.

After a provider-cmdlet or reg.exe write other than deleting Hidden, does Explorer's effective setting change in a fresh process (SHGetSetSettings)? Only the deleted-Hidden case was read (showAll 1 to 0). The other write members were verified at the registry-value level only.
